title: Why “Was $999, Now $499” Works on You
subtitle: 為什麼「原價 999、現在 499」對你有效？定錨效應與損失規避
source: 原創議題文章；依 Wikipedia〈Anchoring effect〉〈Loss aversion〉〈Endowment effect〉所整理之 Tversky & Kahneman（1974, 1979）與 Kahneman, Knetsch & Thaler（1990）研究，2026-10-22 核對

sources.title: Nobel Prize: Daniel Kahneman — Facts (Economic Sciences 2002)

beginner.title: The First Number Wins
paras: You see a jacket in a shop. The sign says: “Was $999, now $499!” It feels like a great deal. But is $499 really cheap? Maybe the jacket was never worth $999. The first number you saw is changing how you think.
你在店裡看到一件外套，標示寫著：「原價 999 元，現在 499 元！」感覺很划算。但 499 元真的便宜嗎？也許這件外套從來就不值 999 元。你看到的第一個數字，正在改變你的想法。

Psychologists call this the “anchoring effect”. An anchor holds a ship in one place. In the same way, the first number we see holds our mind in one place. Our later guesses stay close to it, even when it has nothing to do with the question.
心理學家把這叫作「定錨效應」。船錨能把船固定在一個地方；同樣地，我們看到的第一個數字，也會把思緒固定在一個地方。之後的猜測都會停留在它附近，即使那個數字和問題毫無關係。

In a famous experiment, two psychologists, Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman, showed people a wheel. It stopped on either 10 or 65. Then people guessed what percentage of countries in the United Nations were in Africa. People who saw 10 guessed about 25%. People who saw 65 guessed about 45%. In another study, students were asked if Gandhi died before or after the age of 9. That is clearly wrong! But later these students guessed he died at about 50, while students asked about the age of 140 guessed about 67.
在一個有名的實驗中，兩位心理學家阿莫斯．特沃斯基和丹尼爾．康納曼讓人們看一個轉盤，轉盤會停在 10 或 65。接著，人們要猜聯合國會員國中有百分之幾在非洲。看到 10 的人平均猜 25%；看到 65 的人平均猜 45%。在另一項研究中，學生被問到甘地是在 9 歲之前還是之後去世的。這顯然是錯的！但後來這些學生猜他大約 50 歲去世，而被問到 140 歲的學生則猜大約 67 歲。

The same researchers found something else: losing feels worse than winning feels good. Losing $100 hurts more than finding $100 makes us happy. They called this “loss aversion”. That is why shops say “Don’t miss out!” or “Only today!”
同樣這兩位研究者還發現了另一件事：失去的痛苦，比得到的快樂更強烈。丟掉 100 元的難過，比撿到 100 元的開心更大。他們稱之為「損失規避」。這就是為什麼商店會說「別錯過！」或「只限今天！」。

In 2002, Kahneman won the Nobel Prize in economics for this kind of work. His ideas can help you be a smarter shopper. Before you buy, forget the “was” price. Ask yourself: “Would I pay $499 for this if I never saw the first number?”
2002 年，康納曼因為這類研究獲得諾貝爾經濟學獎。他的觀點能幫助你成為更聰明的消費者。購買之前，先忘掉「原價」。問問自己：「如果我從沒看過第一個數字，我會願意為它付 499 元嗎？」

intermediate.title: Why “Was $999, Now $499” Works on You
paras: A price tag that reads “Was $999, now $499” is not just information. It is a carefully designed signal. The higher number makes the lower one feel like a bargain, even if no one ever paid $999. Behavioural scientists have studied this trick for decades, and their findings reveal two powerful habits of the human mind.
一張寫著「原價 999、現在 499」的價格標籤，不只是資訊，而是精心設計的訊號。較高的數字讓較低的數字感覺像撿到便宜，即使從來沒有人付過 999 元。行為科學家研究這個手法已經幾十年，他們的發現揭露了人類心智的兩個強大習慣。

The first is the anchoring effect: our estimates are pulled towards the first number we encounter. In one early study by Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman, participants had five seconds to estimate the product of the numbers one to eight. When the sequence was written starting with 1 × 2 × 3, the median estimate was 512. When it started with 8 × 7 × 6, the median was 2,250. The correct answer is 40,320.
第一個是定錨效應：我們的估計會被最先遇到的數字拉過去。在阿莫斯．特沃斯基和丹尼爾．康納曼的一項早期研究中，參與者有五秒鐘估計 1 到 8 的連乘積。當算式從 1 × 2 × 3 開始寫，估計的中位數是 512；從 8 × 7 × 6 開始時，中位數是 2,250。正確答案是 40,320。

Even obviously irrelevant numbers can act as anchors. In another study, participants watched a wheel that was set to stop on either 10 or 65, and then estimated the percentage of African countries in the United Nations. Those who saw 10 guessed 25% on average; those who saw 65 guessed 45%. A meaningless number had shifted a factual judgement by twenty points. In a study by Dan Ariely, people first wrote down the last two digits of their social security number and then bid for items such as wine and chocolate. Those with higher digits tended to bid more.
即使是明顯不相關的數字，也能成為錨點。在另一項研究中，參與者先看一個被設定成停在 10 或 65 的轉盤，接著估計聯合國中非洲國家所占的百分比。看到 10 的人平均猜 25%，看到 65 的人平均猜 45%。一個毫無意義的數字，就讓一個事實判斷移動了二十個百分點。在丹．艾瑞利的一項研究中，人們先寫下自己社會安全號碼的最後兩位數，再為葡萄酒和巧克力等商品出價。數字較大的人，出價往往也比較高。

The second habit is loss aversion, a term Kahneman and Tversky introduced in 1979. Losses tend to feel roughly twice as powerful as equivalent gains. A related finding is the endowment effect: in a classic 1990 experiment, students who were given a mug asked for about $7 to sell it, while others were willing to pay only about $3 to buy one. Simply owning the mug made it feel more valuable.
第二個習慣是損失規避，這是康納曼和特沃斯基在 1979 年提出的詞。損失的感受，往往大約是同等收穫的兩倍。一個相關的發現是稟賦效應：在 1990 年的一項經典實驗中，拿到馬克杯的學生要價約 7 美元才肯賣，其他人卻只願意花約 3 美元買一個。光是擁有這個杯子，就讓它感覺更有價值。

Marketers use both habits. A high “original” price sets an anchor, and phrases such as “Only three left!” turn not buying into a kind of loss. Kahneman, who received the Nobel Prize in economics in 2002, showed that these reactions are not signs of stupidity but normal features of human thinking. Knowing about them is the first step towards making choices on purpose rather than by reflex.
行銷人員兩種習慣都會利用。高高的「原價」設下錨點，而像「只剩三件！」這樣的字眼，讓「不買」變成一種損失。2002 年獲得諾貝爾經濟學獎的康納曼證明，這些反應不是愚蠢的表現，而是人類思考的正常特徵。了解它們，是讓自己有意識地做選擇、而不是憑反射做選擇的第一步。

advanced.title: Anchors, Losses and the Limits of Rational Choice
paras: Traditional economics long assumed that people evaluate prices and risks more or less rationally, weighing costs and benefits according to stable preferences. A price tag reading “Was $999, now $499” challenges that assumption. The crossed-out figure supplies no information about the jacket’s quality, yet it reliably makes the second number feel like a bargain. Much of the research explaining why began with the Israeli psychologists Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman, whose work helped found the field now known as behavioural economics.
傳統經濟學長期假設，人們大致上會理性地評估價格與風險，依照穩定的偏好權衡成本與效益。一張寫著「原價 999、現在 499」的價格標籤，挑戰了這個假設。被劃掉的數字對外套的品質毫無說明，卻能穩定地讓第二個數字感覺像撿到便宜。解釋其原因的許多研究，始於以色列心理學家阿莫斯．特沃斯基與丹尼爾．康納曼，他們的研究幫助奠定了今天稱為行為經濟學的領域。

Their concept of anchoring describes how an initial value biases subsequent estimates, because people adjust away from it insufficiently. In one study, participants were given five seconds to estimate the product of the integers from one to eight. Those who saw the sequence in ascending order produced a median estimate of 512; those who saw it in descending order, beginning with the larger numbers, produced a median of 2,250. Both groups were wildly wrong — the true answer is 40,320 — but each was pulled towards the numbers it had happened to see first.
他們提出的定錨概念，描述了一個初始數值如何讓後續的估計產生偏差，因為人們從它出發做的調整不夠多。在一項研究中，參與者有五秒鐘估計 1 到 8 的整數連乘積。看到遞增順序的人，估計中位數是 512；看到遞減順序、從大數字開始的人，中位數是 2,250。兩組都錯得離譜——正確答案是 40,320——但兩組都被自己剛好先看到的數字拉了過去。

More striking is the power of anchors that are plainly irrelevant. Participants who watched a wheel predetermined to stop at 10 or 65 subsequently estimated the percentage of African countries in the United Nations at 25% and 45% respectively. In another study, students asked whether Gandhi died before or after the age of 9, or before or after 140, later gave average estimates of 50 and 67. It is worth adding, however, that a small number of studies using clearly random procedures, such as rolling a die, have failed to reproduce the effect, suggesting that participants may sometimes treat an anchor as a hint.

更驚人的是那些明顯不相關的錨點所具有的力量。看過預設停在 10 或 65 的轉盤的參與者，之後估計聯合國中非洲國家的比例，分別是 25% 和 45%。在另一項研究中，被問到甘地是在 9 歲之前或之後、或 140 歲之前或之後去世的學生，之後給出的平均估計分別是 50 歲和 67 歲。不過值得補充的是，少數使用明顯隨機程序（例如擲骰子）的研究，未能重現這個效應，這表示參與者有時可能把錨點當成一種提示。

A second pillar of the research programme is loss aversion, introduced in Kahneman and Tversky’s prospect theory in 1979. Empirically, losses tend to be weighted roughly twice as heavily as equivalent gains. The related endowment effect was demonstrated in a classic 1990 study by Kahneman, Jack Knetsch and Richard Thaler, in which students who owned a mug demanded about $7 to part with it, while buyers offered only about $3. Not every scholar accepts the universality of loss aversion; some argue that many apparent examples are better explained by psychological inertia, while later studies have replicated the pattern in several samples.

這項研究計畫的第二根支柱，是康納曼與特沃斯基在 1979 年展望理論中提出的損失規避。從實證來看，損失的權重往往大約是同等收穫的兩倍。相關的稟賦效應，則在康納曼、傑克．奈奇與理查．塞勒 1990 年的一項經典研究中得到證明：擁有馬克杯的學生要價約 7 美元才肯割愛，買家卻只出價約 3 美元。並非每位學者都接受損失規避的普遍性；有些人主張許多看似的例子，用心理惰性來解釋更好，而後來的研究也在數個樣本中重現了這個模式。

For consumers, the practical implications are clear. Retailers set anchors with inflated reference prices and frame inaction as loss through countdown timers and warnings that stock is running out. Kahneman, awarded the Nobel Prize in economics in 2002, did not conclude that people are foolish; rather, he showed that intuitive judgement follows predictable patterns. Recognising those patterns cannot make us perfectly rational, but it allows us to pause, question the first number we see and ask whether a choice reflects our own priorities or someone else’s design.
對消費者來說，實際意涵很清楚。零售商用灌水的參考價格設下錨點，並透過倒數計時和「庫存快沒了」的警告，把「不行動」包裝成損失。2002 年獲頒諾貝爾經濟學獎的康納曼，並沒有下結論說人很愚蠢；而是證明了直覺判斷遵循可預測的模式。認識這些模式，無法讓我們變得完全理性，卻能讓我們停下來、質疑看到的第一個數字，並問問自己：這個選擇反映的是自己的優先順序，還是別人的設計？

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How Gandhi became famous around the world.
How to find the cheapest jacket in a shop.
Why countries in Africa joined the United Nations.
How first numbers and fear of losing affect our choices.
beginner.evidence: The first number you saw is changing how you think.
beginner.why: 全文：定錨效應與損失規避如何影響判斷與消費。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：甘地的年齡只是實驗題目。
以偏概全：外套只是開頭的例子。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：聯合國的問題只是實驗題目。

beginner.q: Why do psychologists use the word “anchor” for this effect?
options: Ships use numbers to find their way.
The first number holds our mind in one place.
The price tag is heavy and hard to move.
Shops are often found near the sea.
beginner.evidence: In the same way, the first number we see holds our mind in one place.
beginner.why: 第二段：錨把船固定在一處，第一個數字也把想法固定住。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：船只是比喻的來源，重點在錨把船固定住。
字面誤讀：不是說價錢很重。
字面誤讀：錨只是比喻，不是說商店在海邊。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Students asked about age 9 guessed Gandhi died at about 67.
People who saw 10 on the wheel guessed about 45%.
People who saw 65 on the wheel guessed about 45%.
Kahneman won the Nobel Prize in 1979.
traps: 數字錯位：被問 9 歲的人猜約 50 歲，問 140 歲的人才猜 67。
數字錯位：看到 10 的人猜 25%。
數字錯位：得獎是 2002 年。

beginner.q: What does the writer advise shoppers to do?
options: Ignore the “was” price when deciding what to pay.
Buy quickly before the item is gone.
Always choose the most expensive item in the shop.
Compare prices only on the day of the sale.
beginner.evidence: Before you buy, forget the “was” price.
traps: 正反顛倒：這正是商家利用損失規避的話術。
捏造：作者反而提醒別被高價影響。
捏造：文中沒有談比價的時機。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Anchoring and loss aversion are normal habits that marketers use.
People always choose prices rationally when shopping.
Wine and chocolate are cheaper with a social security number.
Kahneman proved that shoppers are stupid.
intermediate.why: 第一段預告兩種習慣，第五段說商家兩者都用。
traps: 正反顛倒：研究顯示判斷會被干擾。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：酒和巧克力是 Ariely 的實驗物品。
正反顛倒：原文 not signs of stupidity。

intermediate.q: What does the phrase “irrelevant numbers” in the third paragraph mean?
options: Numbers printed on price tags.
Numbers that are too large to count.
Numbers that have nothing to do with the question.
Numbers that give the correct answer.
intermediate.evidence: A meaningless number had shifted a factual judgement by twenty points.
intermediate.why: 轉盤數字和非洲國家比例毫無關係，卻改變了估計。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：價格標籤是另一個例子。
捏造：大小不是重點。
正反顛倒：它們跟正確答案沒有關係。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Buyers were willing to pay about $7 for a mug.
Students who owned a mug asked for about $7 to sell it.
The correct answer to the multiplication problem was 2,250.
Loss aversion was introduced in 2002.
intermediate.evidence: students who were given a mug asked for about $7 to sell it
traps: 數字錯位：買方只願出約 3 美元。
數字錯位：2,250 是估計中位數，正解是 40,320。
數字錯位：1979 年提出，2002 年是得諾貝爾獎。

intermediate.q: Why does a phrase such as “Only three left!” work on shoppers?
options: It proves the item is popular.
It shows the true value of the item.
It lowers the original price.
It makes not buying feel like a loss.
intermediate.evidence: phrases such as “Only three left!” turn not buying into a kind of loss
traps: 過度推論：文中沒這樣說。
捏造：它不提供商品價值的資訊。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：原價是另一種手法（錨點）。

advanced.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To prove that traditional economics was completely correct.
To explain how predictable biases shape judgement and how sellers use them.
To show that every anchoring study has been replicated.
To describe the life of Richard Thaler.
advanced.evidence: he showed that intuitive judgement follows predictable patterns
advanced.why: 全文：定錨與損失規避，以及商家的運用。
traps: 正反顛倒：研究正是在挑戰傳統經濟學的假設。
正反顛倒：有少數研究無法重現。
以偏概全：Thaler 只是馬克杯研究的作者之一。

advanced.q: What does “adjust away from it insufficiently” in the second paragraph mean?
options: People move far beyond the first value.
People ignore the first value completely.
People always guess the correct answer.
People move too little from the first value.
advanced.evidence: because people adjust away from it insufficiently
advanced.why: 從初始值調整得不夠，所以估計被拉向它。
traps: 正反顛倒：是調整得太少。
正反顛倒：問題正是沒有忽略它。
正反顛倒：兩組都錯得很離譜。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Some studies using a die failed to reproduce the anchoring effect.
Losses are weighted about half as heavily as gains.
All scholars agree that loss aversion is universal.
The mug study was carried out in 1979.
advanced.evidence: have failed to reproduce the effect
traps: 數字錯位：損失約是收益的兩倍重。
正反顛倒：原文 Not every scholar accepts the universality。
數字錯位：馬克杯研究在 1990 年。

advanced.q: What does the author suggest readers can gain by recognising these patterns?
options: A way to make retailers lower their prices.
The power to become perfectly rational in every choice.
The ability to pause and question the first number they see.
A method for winning a prize like Kahneman’s Nobel.
advanced.evidence: it allows us to pause, question the first number we see
traps: 捏造：作者說的是改變自己的反應，不是讓商家降價。
正反顛倒：原文 cannot make us perfectly rational。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：諾貝爾獎是 Kahneman 的成就，不是讀者的收穫。

一張寫著「原價 999 元，現價 499 元」的價格標籤，不只是在提供資訊。被劃掉的數字完全沒說明外套的品質，卻總能讓第二個數字感覺像撿到便宜。傳統經濟學長久以來假設，人們判斷價格時大致是理性的。而解釋人們為什麼常常不理性的研究，很多是從兩位以色列心理學家特沃斯基和康納曼開始的——他們的研究幫助奠定了今天所說的行為經濟學。

Their idea of anchoring describes how a first number pulls later estimates towards it, because people do not adjust away from it enough. In one study, participants had five seconds to estimate the product of the numbers from one to eight. Those who saw the numbers in rising order gave a median estimate of 512; those who saw them in falling order gave 2,250. So different were the two answers that the order alone seemed to decide them — and both were wildly wrong, since the true figure is 40,320.
他們提出的「定錨」概念，描述第一個數字如何把之後的估計拉向自己，因為人們從它那裡調整得不夠。在一項研究中，參與者有五秒鐘估計 1 乘到 8 的結果。看到數字由小到大排列的人，估計的中位數是 512；看到由大到小的人是 2,250。兩組差距大到彷彿光是順序就決定了答案——而兩組都錯得離譜，因為正確答案是 40,320。

More striking is the power of numbers that are plainly irrelevant. Participants who watched a wheel set to stop at either 10 or 65 later estimated the percentage of African countries in the United Nations at 25 and 45 percent respectively. It is worth adding, however, that a few studies using clearly random methods, such as rolling a die, have failed to reproduce the effect, which suggests that people may sometimes treat an anchor as a hint.
更驚人的是那些明顯毫不相關的數字的力量。看了停在 10 或 65 的轉盤後，參與者估計聯合國中非洲國家所占的比例，分別是 25% 和 45%。不過值得補充的是，有少數研究用明顯隨機的方法（例如擲骰子）時，沒能重現這個效應，這顯示人們有時可能把錨點當成一種暗示。

A second pillar of the research is loss aversion (the tendency to feel losses more strongly than equal gains), which Kahneman and Tversky introduced in 1979. Losses tend to weigh roughly twice as heavily as gains of the same size. A related finding came from a 1990 study in which students who owned a mug asked for about $7 to sell it, while buyers offered only about $3. Not every scholar accepts that loss aversion is universal, yet later studies have repeated the pattern in several groups.
這項研究的第二根支柱是損失規避（覺得損失比同等的收穫更強烈的傾向），由康納曼和特沃斯基在 1979 年提出。損失的分量，大約是同樣大小的收穫的兩倍。一個相關的發現來自 1990 年的研究：擁有馬克杯的學生，要大約 7 美元才肯賣，而買方只願出大約 3 美元。並非每位學者都接受損失規避是普遍現象，但後來的研究在好幾個族群中重現了這個模式。

Retailers use both habits. They set anchors with inflated “original” prices, and they make not buying feel like a loss through countdown timers and warnings that stock is running out. Kahneman, who received the Nobel Prize in economics in 2002, did not conclude that people are foolish; he showed that our quick judgements follow predictable patterns. Knowing those patterns cannot make us perfectly rational, but it allows us to pause and question the first number we see.
商家兩種習慣都會利用。他們用灌水的「原價」設下錨點，再用倒數計時器和「庫存快沒了」的警告，讓不買感覺像一種損失。2002 年獲得諾貝爾經濟學獎的康納曼，並沒有下結論說人很愚蠢；他證明的是，我們的直覺判斷遵循可預測的模式。了解這些模式無法讓我們完全理性，卻能讓我們停下來，質疑眼前的第一個數字。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How students decide what a coffee mug is worth.
How to calculate the product of the numbers one to eight.
Why most African countries joined the United Nations.
How anchoring and loss aversion shape our judgements of prices.
questions.why: 全文：定錨效應與損失規避如何影響判斷，以及商家如何利用。
traps: 以偏概全：馬克杯只是一個例子。
以偏概全：乘法估計只是實驗題目。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：聯合國問題只是轉盤實驗的題目。

questions.q: What does “inflated” mean in “inflated “original” prices” in the last paragraph?
options: Printed in large and colourful letters.
Made higher than they really should be.
Changed every day by a countdown timer.
Calculated carefully from real costs.
questions.evidence: They set anchors with inflated “original” prices
questions.why: 商家故意把「原價」灌高，讓現價看起來很便宜。
traps: 字面誤讀：inflate 原意是充氣，不是字變大。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：倒數計時器是另一個手法。
正反顛倒：灌水的價格並非依實際成本。

questions.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The true product of one to eight is 2,250.
Buyers offered about $7 for the mug.
Owners of the mug asked for about $7 to sell it.
Kahneman received the Nobel Prize in 1979.
questions.evidence: students who owned a mug asked for about $7 to sell it
traps: 數字錯位：2,250 是估計中位數，正確答案是 40,320。
數字錯位：買方只出約 3 美元。
數字錯位：1979 年提出損失規避，2002 年得獎。

Warning that stock is running out.

traps: 有提到：inflated “original” prices。
有提到：countdown timers。
有提到：warnings that stock is running out。

mixed.q: Which of the following are stated in the passage? Choose ALL that apply.
options: Rising-order viewers gave a median estimate of 512.
The wheel was set to stop at 10 or 65.
Every study has reproduced the anchoring effect.
Losses weigh about twice as much as equal gains.
All scholars agree loss aversion is universal.
Kahneman concluded that people are foolish.
mixed.why: A 第二段；B 第三段；D 第四段。C 正反顛倒（擲骰子的研究沒能重現）；E 正反顛倒（並非每位學者都接受）；F 正反顛倒（他沒有這樣下結論）。
